subject.title: [Feature]: Memory importance scoring + time decay for long-term memory

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable importance/decay contract to the active memory plugin surface, and if so which schema, scoring policy, backends, and config knobs should own it?
rationale: The issue is not a narrow bug: it changes persisted memory semantics, public configuration, QMD/LanceDB/builtin parity, and contradiction handling, which automation should not choose independently.

options.title: Design plugin-owned importance contract
options.body: Add a generic active-memory plugin contract for importance metadata, scoring, decay/access reinforcement, and supersession semantics, then implement it across supported memory paths.

options.title: Prototype memory-core only
options.body: Limit the first iteration to memory-core hybrid retrieval with explicit docs that QMD and external memory plugins are not yet covered.

options.title: Defer to external plugins
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core unchanged until multi-slot memory or a ClawHub memory plugin proves the policy outside core.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned importance contract
recommendation.body: Add a generic active-memory plugin contract for importance metadata, scoring, decay/access reinforcement, and supersession semantics, then implement it across supported memory paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available owner signal for memory plugin boundaries and recent memory-core refactors among the identified likely owners.
